Welcome to CJJA

Training for everyone, built to match your goals

We strive to be a friendly, clean, safe, family-focused, and no-nonsense gym. We teach Gi and No-Gi Jiu-Jitsu and Wrestling for defense, sport, fitness, and fun. As an unaffiliated school, we welcome practitioners from all walks of life and all fitness and experience levels.

At CJJA, we prioritize technique and fluidity over strength, speed, and aggression. Rather than a one-size-fits-all approach, we equip students with core grappling skills while helping them develop a style that suits their body and personality.

You’ll find us in the Lake Norman area on Chartwell Center Drive, just minutes off I-77 — an easy drive from Huntersville, Davidson, Mooresville, and beyond. We love Jiu-Jitsu and would be honored to help you on your way — let’s roll!

Good to Know

Frequently asked questions

What should I bring to my first class?

On gi days we train in a uniform called a “gi” — long pants, a jacket, and a belt. We have plenty on hand for you to borrow, and if you have your own, any color, brand, or affiliation patches are welcome. On no-gi days, shorts without pockets and a compression shirt (rash guard) are preferred. A water bottle and flip-flops are a good call as well.

Can I try it out before joining?

Yep! Just see one of our instructors or members to fill out a contact form and waiver, and you’re good to go for a free week of training.

Can I train here if I go to another academy?

Yep! We don’t go in for gym drama. We just want to train. Come visit class, come to Open Mat. We are Switzerland… neutral.

Do I need to be in shape?

In short… no. For most people, Jiu-Jitsu is completely different from any activity, sport, or exercise they’ve ever done. Whether you are straight off the couch or right out of the CrossFit gym, Jiu-Jitsu is a cardio, strength, and mental workout that you simply can’t prepare for. The only way to get in shape for Jiu-Jitsu is to do Jiu-Jitsu.

What about etiquette?

We’re not concerned with bowing, and you don’t need permission to come onto the mats. We care most about respecting the space and your training partners:

  • Don’t be stinky — wash your gear (gi, shorts, rash guard, AND belt) between every session.
  • Trim your nails; no shoes on the mat, no bare feet in the bathroom (hint: wear flip-flops).
  • Respect your partners and coaches — if tempers flare, both athletes leave the mats.
  • Don’t give any more than you want to get. No slamming, gouging, pinching, slapping, punching, or kicking.
Where are you located?

We’re at 20488 Chartwell Center Drive in Cornelius, NC, just off I-77. If you’re coming from Huntersville, Davidson, or Mooresville, we’re only a few exits away.
